input: s is lowercase ASCII with length in [1,1000]. indices,sources,targets are parallel Arrays of equal length M in [0,100]. Each index is in [0,len(s)-1], and each source/target is lowercase ASCII of length 1 through 50. All source intervals that actually match the ORIGINAL s are pairwise disjoint. Empty operation lists are accepted. Integer inputs, when present, are primitive safe-integer Numbers excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The string produced by simultaneously replacing every matching source at its original index with the corresponding target. Nonmatching operations do nothing. Operations are checked against original s, never against earlier replacements, and output-length changes do not shift other original indices.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. The match map and output-part Array are private. No input array is sorted, rewritten or shortened; returned strings are immutable and fresh string identity is not promised.
numeric: Indices, lengths and output cursor arithmetic are exact small integers. Every successful source is nonempty, so applying a match strictly advances the original-string cursor. At most 100 replacements of at most 50 characters keep output length <=6000.
complexity: O(L+sum(source lengths)+output length+M) time under ordinary map operations; O(M+L+output length+1) auxiliary/output storage including map, part references and joined string. startswith/startsWith comparisons are charged and bounded by source lengths. No repeated whole-string replacement or sorting is used. Map/set operation costs assume ordinary average O(1) lookup; target-runtime behavior must be qualified, and universal ECMAScript constant-time guarantees or adversarial collision resistance are not claimed.
